    Ported from TauCeti (TauCeti.RepresentationTheory.Quiver.Representation.AsModule, commit 580b6f9d5, Apache 2.0).

    The module over the path algebra carried by a representation of a quiver #

    LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.RepresentationTheory.Quiver.Representation.OfModule turns a left module over the path algebra kQ of a finite quiver into a representation of Q, and proves that functor fully faithful. This file supplies the other half: the kQ-module LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep.asModule carried by a representation, the identification of its vertex components with the vertex spaces of the representation one started from, and hence the essential surjectivity that completes the equivalence

    LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.quiverRepEquivalence : QuiverRep k Q ≌ ModuleCat (pathAlgebra k Q).

    The construction #

    The carrier is the direct sum ⨁ᵥ Mᵥ of the vertex spaces. A basis path p : a ⟶ b of kQ acts on it by the endomorphism LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep.pathEnd that reads off the a-component, applies the structure map M.map p, and puts the result in the b-component; two such endomorphisms compose to the endomorphism of the concatenated path when the paths meet (LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep.pathEnd_mul_pathEnd_of_comp) and to zero when they do not (LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep.pathEnd_mul_pathEnd_of_not_composable), while the trivial paths give the component projections, which sum to the identity (LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep.sum_pathEnd_nil). Those are exactly the three hypotheses of the universal property LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.PathAlgebra.liftAlgHom, so the assignment extends to an algebra homomorphism LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep.toEnd : kQ →ₐ[k] End_k (⨁ᵥ Mᵥ), and LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep.asModule is ⨁ᵥ Mᵥ with the module structure it induces.

    With that in hand the vertex idempotent eᵥ acts as the composite of the projection to Mᵥ and the inclusion back (LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep.vertexIdempotent_smul), so the vertex component eᵥ · asModule is exactly the image of Mᵥ (LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep.vertexComponent_asModule) and the inclusion is a k-linear isomorphism onto it, LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep.vertexComponentEquiv. Those isomorphisms are natural in the path, because a path acts on the image of Mₐ through M.map p (LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep.ofPath_smul_ofVertex, whence LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep.pathMap_vertexComponentEquiv); assembling them with CategoryTheory.NatIso.ofComponents gives the natural isomorphism LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep.asModuleIso. Transported to the model LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep.asModuleShrink of the carrier in the universe of the representation itself, that isomorphism becomes LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep.asModuleShrinkIso, the essential surjectivity of LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.quiverRepFunctor.

    Main definitions #

    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep.pathEnd: the endomorphism of ⨁ᵥ Mᵥ by which a basis path of kQ acts, and LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep.toEnd: that action extended along the path basis as a k-algebra homomorphism into End_k (⨁ᵥ Mᵥ).
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep.asModule: the kQ-module carried by a representation of Q, the direct sum ⨁ᵥ Mᵥ with the action of LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep.toEnd.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep.ofVertex and LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep.toVertex: the inclusion of a vertex space into that module and the projection onto it.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep.asModuleShrink: the model of that module in the universe of the representation, LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep.asModuleShrinkEquiv identifying the two.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.quiverRepEquivalence: representations of a quiver are modules over its path algebra, with LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.quiverRepEquivalenceFunctorObjShrinkIso identifying the module it sends a representation to with LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep.asModuleShrink, and LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.quiverRepEquivalenceFunctorObjIso identifying it with LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep.asModule itself in the universe where the direct sum lives.

    Main results #

    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep.ofPath_smul: a basis path acts on asModule by reading off the component at its source, applying the structure map and putting the result in the component at its target; the two cases used below are LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep.ofPath_smul_ofVertex and LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep.vertexIdempotent_smul, the latter saying that the vertex idempotent eᵥ acts as the projection onto the summand Mᵥ, whence LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep.vertexComponent_asModule: the vertex component of asModule at v is the image of Mᵥ.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep.vertexComponentEquiv: the vertex space Mᵥ is that vertex component, and LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep.pathMap_vertexComponentEquiv: the identification is natural in the path.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep.asModuleIso: the representation carried by asModule M is M, whence LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep.asModuleShrinkIso says the same of the small model, so LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.quiverRepFunctor is essentially surjective, and being fully faithful already it is an equivalence. LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep.dimVector_asModule records that the dimension vector is unchanged.

    Implementation notes #

    The vertex spaces are used through the family LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep.vertexSpace of LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.RepresentationTheory.Quiver.Representation.Basic rather than as M.obj v directly, because instance search does not see the objects of CategoryTheory.Paths Q as vertices when it is asked for the family of instances that a direct sum indexed by the vertices needs; that file's implementation notes say more. For the same reason the naturality squares of LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep.asModuleIso and LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep.asModuleShrinkIso open with change Q at a, restating their quantified objects as vertices.

    The k-module structure on LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep.asModule is deliberately not the one the direct sum already carries: it is Module.restrictScalars k (pathAlgebra k Q), restriction of scalars along algebraMap. That is exactly the structure ModuleCat.moduleOfAlgebraModule puts on an object of ModuleCat (kQ), which is the one LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.quiverRepFunctor uses; taking the direct sum's own structure instead would give a second, only propositionally equal, Module k instance and the essential-surjectivity isomorphism would not typecheck against the functor. That the two agree is what makes the identification LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep.asModuleEquiv with the direct sum k-linear; the identity additive equivalence it upgrades is private, asModuleEquiv being the identification consumers use.

    DecidableEq Q is needed to write down the summand inclusions DirectSum.lof, so it is carried through the construction; the essential-surjectivity instance is a Prop and discharges it with classical, so neither it nor LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.quiverRepEquivalence asks for it.

    The concrete carrier is indexed by Q : Type v with summands in Type t, so ⨁ᵥ Mᵥ : Type (max v t): LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep.asModule lands in a larger universe than the representation it is built from whenever the vertex type does. LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.quiverRepEquivalence is nevertheless stated at an arbitrary representation universe t, because over a finite vertex set that direct sum is a finite product of the vertex spaces and so has a model in Type t (LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep.small_asModule); the model LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep.asModuleShrink of it, whose vertex components are those of asModule because LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.QuiverRep.asModuleShrinkEquiv is kQ-linear, is what witnesses essential surjectivity there; LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.quiverRepEquivalence's forward direction is identified with that model by LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.quiverRepEquivalenceFunctorObjShrinkIso. The concrete direct-sum API is kept at max v t, and LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.quiverRepEquivalenceFunctorObjIso identifies the forward direction with asModule itself at that universe.

    References #

    The plan of the file follows Mathlib's group-algebra analogue: the type synonym carrying a module structure through Module.compHom, the equivalence with the underlying type and the shape of the final ≌ ModuleCat (algebra) statement are those of Representation.asModule, Representation.asModuleEquiv and Rep.equivalenceModuleMonoidAlgebra for k[G].

    See I. Assem, D. Simson, A. Skowroński, Elements of the Representation Theory of Associative Algebras, Vol. 1, Ch. III, or R. Schiffler, Quiver Representations, Ch. 5.
